llm.summary: This is a disclosed VMware audit and policy helper that stores local audit data, with no hidden exfiltration or destructive behavior found in the reviewed artifacts.

dimensions.detail: The skill documents local-only SQLite audit storage, optional rules under ~/.vmware or OPS_HOME, read-only agent detection by environment variable presence, and no runtime network/webhook use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses uv to install the vmware-policy package and requires Bash/uvx; this is disclosed and versioned, though the package code is external to the inspected markdown artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to querying audit logs, configuring policy rules, and integrating the decorator; the reference guardrails are broad guidance for VMware-family skills, but not hidden prompt hijacking.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent local audit, rules, and undo databases are expected for the audit/policy purpose and are disclosed; users should note that audit writes are best-effort and VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 is an operator-controlled policy bypass.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is audit logging, optional policy enforcement, and input sanitization for VMware-related skills; the documented CLI/library capabilities match that purpose and the artifact says it exposes no MCP tools itself.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want the VMware skill family to keep local audit records and optional policy rules. Treat ~/.vmware/audit.db and rotated archives as confidential because they may contain infrastructure names, parameters, results, and redacted operational data. Configure rules.yaml or an approval workflow before relying on it to block production changes, and restrict who can set VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The kubeconfig/token/password references are redaction examples and sensitive-result handling for audit rows, not evidence that the skill reads credential files.
[PE2] expected: The chmod examples set restrictive permissions on the local ~/.vmware directory and audit database; they do not invoke sudo or root escalation.
[RA2] expected: The ~/.vmware audit.db, rules.yaml, and undo.db files are disclosed local state for audit and policy behavior, not an unauthorized background persistence mechanism.
[EA2] expected: The artifacts do disclose that default policy rules deny nothing and that human approval requires configured rules or vmware-pilot; this is a security-posture note rather than hidden autonomous behavior in this skill.
[E3] expected: The filesystem command is a scoped troubleshooting check for ~/.vmware/rules.yaml, not broad local file enumeration.
